instruction.name: vmod.b
instruction.description: Compute the remainder of each signed 8-bit element in `a` divided by the corresponding element in `b`.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.init: li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr2, $r4

latencies.notes: Data-dependent, and a ladder rather than a set of discrete classes: latency = 5 + (64/8)*(6 + floor(bits(|quotient|)/4)), that is 5 + 8*(6 + n) with n the number of complete four-bit quotient digits. The minimum is 29 with a zero dividend and the maximum is 69 at a 7-bit quotient. LSX and LASX are identical for every element width although LASX carries twice the lanes, so the lanes and both 128-bit halves are refined in parallel and only the element width sets the per-bit rate, 16 quotient bits per cycle in aggregate. The unit divides magnitudes, skips trailing zero digits (2^40 / 1 still costs 11) and only pays for active lanes (one active lane in vdiv.bu measures 34 against 69 with every lane active). Measured with the drift-free chain `vmod.b $xr0, $xr0, $xr1` and divisor 1, which returns the dividend unchanged. The remainder needs one extra digit, which adds 8 cycles, so the maximum includes it. The cases array holds named sample points on this ladder, not an exhaustive classification.

experiment.name: no active lane or zero dividend
experiment.init: li.d $r4, 0; vreplgr2vr.b $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 0; vreplgr2vr.d $vr2, $r4; li.d $r4, 0; vreplgr2vr.b $vr3, $r4
experiment.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 3 --init 'li.d $r4, 0; vreplgr2vr.b $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 0; vreplgr2vr.d $vr2, $r4; li.d $r4, 0; vreplgr2vr.b $vr3, $r4' --asm 'vmod.b $vr0, $vr0, $vr1'

experiment.name: full-width quotient, all lanes active
experiment.init: li.d $r4, 127; vreplgr2vr.b $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 0; vreplgr2vr.d $vr2, $r4; li.d $r4, 127; vreplgr2vr.b $vr3, $r4
experiment.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 3 --init 'li.d $r4, 127; vreplgr2vr.b $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 0; vreplgr2vr.d $vr2, $r4; li.d $r4, 127; vreplgr2vr.b $vr3, $r4' --asm 'vmod.b $vr0, $vr0, $vr1; vand.v $vr0, $vr0, $vr2; vor.v $vr0, $vr0, $vr3'
experiment.notes: reset helper (vand+vor, 2 cycles) calibrated against the same chain with vand.v in place of the divide; chain_latency = 1.99

throughput.notes: Range over the same pairs: min CPI 13.50 at 0/2, max CPI 33.50 at 127/1. Sample uses 1/1.

notes: LSX variable-latency integer divide/modulo. Latency uses an element-0 reset helper; throughput uses 8 independent lanes. Ranges cover positive operands including powers of two and max values. Both vector sources are recorded separately; they share the same result path where the hardware is symmetric.
